items.title: neutral-stance-not-explained
items.claim: Image #2 asks for one stance input plus one technique input, while Image #6 shows Lunge Punch using the standing dot plus forward without explicitly saying to leave the stance stick centered.
items.reason: A newcomer could interpret the opening instruction as requiring both sticks to be pushed.
items.suggest: Change the instruction to: 'Choose a stance—leave STANCE centered for standing—then push TECHNIQUE.'

items.title: countdown-competes-with-instructions
items.claim: Image #2 displays 'STARTING IN 5' beneath FIGHT while the opponent description and control instructions remain visible.
items.reason: This communicates a deadline for reading; the still cannot establish whether the fight actually starts automatically.
items.suggest: Replace the introductory countdown with 'Start when ready'; verify its behavior and require an explicit FIGHT action on this instructional card.

items.title: score-calls-need-plain-language
items.claim: Images #17 and #20 display IPPON and WAZA-ARI respectively, but neither call banner includes 'full point' or 'half point'.
items.reason: Players unfamiliar with karate terminology must interpret the HUD score instead of learning the award directly from the prominent announcement.
items.suggest: Keep the karate terms and add 'Full point' beneath IPPON and 'Half point' beneath WAZA-ARI.

items.title: desktop-bindings-not-visible
items.claim: Image #9 labels the two desktop joysticks STANCE and TECHNIQUE but shows no keyboard key bindings for either.
items.reason: A keyboard player cannot discover the corresponding keys from the visible play screen.
items.suggest: Display the actual configured keyboard bindings beside each joystick label on desktop, without displacing the primary touch controls.

items.title: fighter-label-size-unverified
items.claim: I cannot determine whether the visible fighter-name labels in Images #3 and #9 satisfy the required 18 CSS px minimum from these raster frames.
items.reason: Those names identify the competitors, and screenshot pixels alone do not establish their rendered CSS sizing.
items.suggest: Measure their computed font sizes and applied scaling at the phone and desktop viewports; enlarge any verified undersized labels and reflow the scoreboard rather than shrinking the text.
